questions.prompt: In Three.js, what does the renderer do?
options: Holds all the objects and lights
Draws what the camera sees onto a <canvas>
Decides which part of the world you see
explanations: That's the scene: the world that contains everything.
Correct: the renderer turns the camera's view into pixels on a canvas.
That's the camera's job.
Loaders (like GLTFLoader in Module 4) load models. The renderer draws.

questions.prompt: Put these lines in order so the cube appears on screen.
explanations: Import Three.js first (everything else uses THREE), create the scene, add the cube to it, and only then render: rendering before adding draws an empty world.
questions.hint: Each line needs the one before it.

questions.prompt: Your cube is at (0, 0, 0) and so is your camera. You see nothing. What's the simplest fix?
options: Set the canvas background to white
explanations: Correct: move the camera back so the cube is in front of it.
The camera is inside the cube; a smaller cube is still around the camera.
One scene is enough. The camera needs to step back.
The background colour doesn't change what the camera can see.

questions.prompt: Which line creates a visible object correctly?
explanations: Correct: a mesh takes a geometry (shape) and a material (surface).
It's the other way round: the mesh contains the geometry.
A material doesn't take a geometry; both go into a Mesh.
A scene is created empty; you add meshes to it with scene.add().

questions.prompt: Spot the bug. Nothing appears on screen. Which line is missing?
options: A line creating a second material
explanations: One material is enough.
Correct: the knot was created but never added to the scene.
Geometries don't render themselves; the renderer draws the scene.
Materials have no show property. The mesh needs adding to the scene.
questions.hint: Is the knot in the world?

questions.prompt: Your MeshStandardMaterial object is completely black. Why?
options: There are no lights in the scene
explanations: Correct: standard materials only show colour where light hits them.
A close camera still sees colour if there's light.
Simple shapes still show colour when lit.
Canvas size doesn't change whether the object is lit.
questions.hint: What do realistic materials need to be seen?

questions.prompt: Which light works like the sun, with parallel rays from one direction?
explanations: Ambient light fills everything evenly, with no direction.
Correct: directional light has parallel rays, like sunlight.
A point light shines outward from one spot, like a bulb.
That's a material that ignores light, not a light.

questions.prompt: Which material ignores lights and always shows its flat colour?
explanations: Standard material reacts to light: it's black in the dark.
Correct: Basic material is unlit, one flat colour.
Physical material is even more realistic than standard, so it needs light too.
Most realistic materials depend on light.
questions.hint: Its name says it's the simplest one.

options: Calls animate once, just before the next screen refresh
Records a video of the canvas
Loads the next frame of a 3D model
explanations: Correct: and calling it again inside animate creates a loop.
It follows the screen's refresh rate (often 60 times a second), not once a second.
It doesn't record anything.
It's a browser timing function, not a model loader.
questions.hint: It's how the loop keeps going, frame after frame.

questions.prompt: How much is a full turn in Three.js rotation units?
explanations: Three.js uses radians, not degrees.
Correct: a full turn is 2π radians, about 6.28.
1 radian is about 57 degrees, not a full turn.
Rotation isn't measured in percent.

questions.prompt: Which CSS makes the 3D canvas a full-screen background behind your content?
explanations: Correct: pinned to the window, full screen, behind everything.
That hides the canvas completely.
Half width is still in the page flow, pushing content around.
z-index 999 puts it on top of your content, covering it.

questions.prompt: After resizing the window, your 3D scene looks stretched. What did you forget?
options: Updating camera.aspect, calling camera.updateProjectionMatrix() and renderer.setSize() on resize
explanations: Correct: the camera and canvas need the new width and height.
Three.js is already loaded; it needs the new size, not a reload.
Lights don't affect stretching.
The shape is fine; the camera's aspect ratio is out of date.
